title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. These policies are intended to: reduce operational risk, ensure compliance, make approvals predictable, and provide a single source of truth for employees and teams.

For team-specific variants (e.g., Dedicated, Private deployments), see the related pages listed above and notify people-ops when exceptions are required.

1) Access and permissions

Summary: All access to corporate systems is granted via role-based policies and approved through a standard request/approval workflow. Key services: Okta (SSO), Google Workspace, AWS IAM, GCP IAM, HashiCorp Vault, GitHub, Slack, Confluence, Jira.

Policy highlights:
- Authentication: SSO via Okta is mandatory for all employees and contractors. MFA (TOTP or security keys) is required for all accounts.
- Least privilege: Access is granted on the principle of least privilege and reviewed quarterly. Teams must define role templates in the Access Catalog (example: eng-servicing-reader, eng-runtime-admin).
- Privileged access: Requests for elevated privileges (e.g., prod IAM, Vault write keys) require an approver from both the owning service team and Security. Approval is logged in the request ticket.
- Temporary access: Temporary access is time-bound. Standard temporary access is 3 business days; emergency access must be requested via PagerDuty escalation and is limited to 4 hours unless extended by security approval.

Request process (standard):
1. Open a request using the Access Request template (Confluence link in templates section).
2. Team manager approves.
3. System owner or role owner approves.
4. Access is provisioned by Identity team within 3 business days.

Escalation & SLA:
- Standard requests: target turnaround 72 hours (3 business days).
- Expedited (business critical): target 8 hours with manager + service owner approval.
- Emergency (security incident): immediate escalation to Security on-call; access duration capped at 4 hours by default.

Ownership and reviews:
- Identity and Access Management (IAM) – eng-infra owns tooling and automation.
- People Ops maintains hiring/leaver workflows integrated with Okta and Google Workspace.
- Quarterly access review: team leads receive automated reports and must attest within 7 days.

2) Change management (applies to infra, runtime, product-facing APIs)

Summary: All changes are classified and handled via risk-based processes. We use a lightweight Change Advisory Board (CAB) for medium/major changes and automated gating for small/non-disruptive changes.

Change classification:
- Standard (low risk): configuration tweaks, documentation updates, non-prod deployments. No CAB review required.
- Minor (medium risk): infra config changes, scaling policy updates, non-user-impacting runtime changes. Requires peer review and scheduled window; CAB notified.
- Major (high risk): schema changes, prod runtime upgrades, database migrations, network changes affecting multiple regions. Requires a formal change request, testing plan, rollback plan, and CAB approval.

Change request template (required fields):
- Change owner, impacted services, proposed window, detailed steps, testing plan, rollback steps, monitoring/runbook pointers, business justification, and approvers.

Approval workflow and timings:
1. Submit Change Request (Jira change ticket) at least 72 hours before planned window for Minor, 7 days for Major.
2. Peer review by service owners and SRE.
3. CAB review (board meets twice weekly); exceptions can be handled asynchronously for tested, automated changes.
4. Post-deploy verification and automated canary metrics must mature for at least one hour before full rollout.

Standard change windows and blackout periods:
- Normal maintenance window: Saturdays 02:00–06:00 UTC for global-impact changes.
- Emergency changes: allowed 24/7 with on-call SRE + incident lead approval.
- Blackout periods: end-of-quarter billing windows, major customer events, and product launch days (see release calendar).

Monitoring & rollback thresholds:
- Latency increase > 50% above baseline for > 5 minutes: trigger automated rollback.
- Error rate increase > 3x baseline for > 5 minutes: trigger incident runbook and roll forward/rollback decision.

3) Data management

Classification:
- Public: data intended for public consumption.
- Internal: non-sensitive business data.
- Confidential: PII, customer-identifiable logs, contract terms.
- Restricted: production secrets, private customer data regulated by contract.

Storage and encryption:
- All data at rest must be encrypted using KMS-managed keys (AWS KMS or GCP KMS).
- Secrets are stored only in HashiCorp Vault with automatic rotation for high-impact keys.
- Databases and object stores must enforce server-side encryption; client-side encryption recommended for restricted datasets.

Retention and deletion:
- Default logs: 90 days.
- Analytics aggregates: 2 years.
- Backups: 30-day rolling snapshots with offsite replication for critical services.
- Customer data: retention per contract; default retention 1 year unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Deletion requests: Data Subject Access Requests (DSARs) are handled by Privacy and Legal; follow the DSAR runbook.

Access controls and auditing:
- Access to restricted data requires business justification and is logged.
- Audit logs: all privilege escalations, data exports, and bulk downloads are logged and retained for at least 1 year.
- Data exfiltration alerting: threshold-based alerts for large-volume exports (e.g., > 10GB in 1 hour).

Data sharing and transfers:
- Cross-border transfers: consult Legal for customer data moving across jurisdictions.
- Third-party processors: require data processing agreements and security attestations (SOC2 or equivalent).

4) Procurement and expenses

Procurement channels and tooling:
- Preferred procurement tool: ServiceNow/Procurement module (or approved alternative).
- Small purchases (<= $5k): team lead approval via expense workflow.
- Medium purchases ($5k–$100k): procurement + finance review, purchase order.
- Large purchases (> $100k): VP-level approval, legal review, and signed contract.

Corporate card and expenses:
- Corporate cards issued by Finance; cardholders must complete training.
- Expense submission: receipts required for all expenses; submit within 30 days.
- Reimbursement SLA: Finance processes valid claims within 10 business days.

PO creation and vendor selection:
1. Initiator submits procurement request with business justification and cost center.
2. Procurement team runs sourcing and recommends vendors; include at least 2 competitive options for > $25k purchases.
3. Finance and Legal review contract terms and SLA.
4. PO issued and goods/services procured.

Spending controls and reconciliations:
- Monthly budget variance reports are sent to each cost center.
- Unexpected spend > $10k requires immediate notification to Finance and the cost center owner.

5) Vendor management

Vendor onboarding checklist:
- Business justification and owner.
- Security questionnaire (completed and reviewed by Security).
- Contract with data processing agreement (if data will be processed).
- Proof of relevant attestations (SOC2, ISO27001) where applicable.
- Insurance and indemnity clauses reviewed by Legal.

Ongoing vendor monitoring:
- Annual review of critical vendors (security posture, performance against SLAs, financial health).
- Quarterly operational checks for key vendors (uptime, incident history).
- Escalation path documented in the vendor record.

Termination and offboarding:
- Offboarding checklist: revoke access, retrieve or delete company data, ensure return of assets, confirm invoice closure.
- Data disposition: follow contract terms and Data Management retention/deletion rules.

6) Travel policy

Booking and approvals:
- Booking tool: TripActions (preferred) or approved travel desk.
- All travel must be pre-approved by the traveler’s manager. International travel requires a second-level approval from People Ops for visa/immigration support.

Allowable expenses and limits:
- Air travel: economy for flights < 6 hours; premium economy/selected business upgrade with manager pre-approval.
- Lodging: choose mid-tier business hotels; maximum per-night rates vary by location (see travel rate table below).
- Per diem: $60 domestic, $120 international (adjust by location—see rate table).

Expense submission and timelines:
- Submit travel expenses within 14 days of trip completion with itemized receipts.
- Currency conversions: use the date of the transaction for conversion rates.

Safety and emergency support:
- Emergency contacts: Security on-call + People Ops travel team.
- Evacuation/assistance: for high-risk regions, coordinate with Security before travel and register the trip with the travel desk.

Travel rate table (examples):
- San Francisco: lodging cap $300/night, per diem $70
- London: lodging cap GBP 180/night, per diem GBP 90
- Berlin: lodging cap EUR 160/night, per diem EUR 80

7) Internal templates and examples

Available templates (Confluence links):
- Access Request template (title: access-request-template).
- Change Request / RFC template (title: change-request-template).
- Vendor Evaluation checklist (title: vendor-eval-template).
- Travel Request + Expense form (title: travel-expense-template).
- Procurement Request (title: procurement-request-template).
- DSAR initiation form (title: dsar-request-template).

How to use templates:
- Copy the template into your team space and fill out required fields before submitting to the central workflow (Jira/ServiceNow integration).
- Each template contains required metadata fields used by automation (owner, impact scope, cost center, approvers).

Governance, exceptions, and contacts

Governance:
- People Ops owns this consolidated policy set and coordinates reviews with Finance, Security, Legal, and Engineering.
- Annual review: policies are reviewed and versioned annually or when material changes occur.

Exceptions:
- Requests for exceptions must be submitted using the Exception Request template and include a compensating controls plan and expiration date.
- Security-related exceptions require Security + Legal sign-off.

Contacts (primary):
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.ai
- Finance (procurement & cards): finance@redwood.ai
- Security: security@redwood.ai
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.ai
- Identity/IAM: iam-team@redwood.ai

Appendices

A. Quick checklists
- New hire onboarding checklist: create Okta account, add Google Workspace, provision Slack, assign baseline role.
- Vendor onboarding: complete security questionnaire, legal sign-off, PO issued.
- Change pre-flight: automated tests, canary config, rollback documented.

B. Example escalation matrix (summary)
- Low severity: assignee -> team lead -> SRE on-call
- Medium severity (service degradation): SRE on-call -> engineering manager -> Tech Lead -> Security if suspected breach
- High severity (customer-impacting or suspected breach): Incident commander -> CTO -> Security -> Legal -> People Ops for communications

C. References and links
- Access control tooling: Okta (https://okta.example.internal), HashiCorp Vault (https://vault.example.internal)
- Procurement platform: ServiceNow Procurement module (https://procurement.example.internal)
- Change management and tickets: Jira change project (JIRA-CHANGES)
- Travel booking: TripActions (https://tripactions.example.internal)

Document history and versioning
- 2024-02-01: Initial consolidated policy (Aisha Patel).
- 2025-09-12: Added temporary access SLA and data exfil alert thresholds (reviewers: Marcus Chen).
- 2026-03-01: Updated procurement thresholds and travel rate table (reviewers: Sofia Rodriguez, Daniel Kim).

If you need a printable checklist, automation snippet, or a tailored team-specific variant, contact People Ops or open an internal ticket.
